newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's bonos ended higher on Friday as further evidence of sustained U.S. economic growth with low inflation put fuel in Euro markets on Friday afternoon.
"The jump we had after U.S. jobs data proved everybody was short here. We saw a real squeeze all around Europe and in Spain as well," said Emilio Sainz at Natwest in Madrid.

But others, even though less pessimistic than a week ago, remained wary of EMU jitters. "After all, we had a positive week in Spain, with positive news from PPI and with good results at the auctions," said Luca Jellinek at Paribas in London.
Last Friday, bono futures ended at 111.70, down 2.09 bps.
"The market remains vulnerable and worried," Jellinek added.
Dealers added both Italian and Spanish market were very well supported by a high level of domestic savings.

"They're plenty of fresh funds and..they are buying on every dip. That's supporting the market," another dealer added. The 10-year spread over Bunds was reduced to around 122 basis points late Friday from around 129 bps this morning.

Ahead of February CPI, Spain's yield curve steepened further. A Reuter poll forecast CPI to show a 0.2 percent monthly increase with the yearly rate declining to 2.8 percent from 2.9 percent in January. The data is expected on Feb 13.
